title: I tried Gemini's free new movie maker; Hollywood has absolutely nothing to worry about
key_facts: Android Police says Google released a new video editing platform, Google Vids, with free use of its AI video generator; there is no mobile app, so it runs on a computer.
The writer describes it as a simple timeline editor, like Windows Movie Maker, but built around AI.
AI options include prompt-to-video, making a video from a Google Docs file, an AI avatar host, and direct edits with a tool called Omni.
The writer tested it with a rough script about an Apple Store employee discovering an Android phone; the AI chose the framing and many odd details, which he found hilarious.
Problems he lists: speech that stutters, shots that do not match each other, and no grasp of how 3D space works.
The 'Extend' feature adds a new clip to the end of a generated video, for up to 20 seconds, but people still teleport and one actor morphs into another.
His verdict: fun, but Hollywood has nothing to fear yet; he is unsure AI video can get past these limits.
quote_evidence: But Hollywood certainly shouldn't be worried yet.
Plus, it can only extend for up to 20 seconds.
If it can't move past that, Hollywood's job is safe.
why_it_matters_hint: Free AI video making is now in a mainstream Google editor, though the reviewer says quality is still far from professional.
notes: One reviewer's hands-on opinion. The pool title says Gemini; the article is about Google Vids. Launch date of the free generator is not stated.
